title: Simplicial model structure on an undercategory
statement:
Use the model-category, simplicial tensor, cotensor and enriched mapping-set conventions of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a simplicial model category and let $A\in\mathcal M$ be any object, not necessarily cofibrant. The ordinary undercategory $\mathcal M_{A/}$ has objects arrows $a:A\to X$ and morphisms $a\to b$ arrows $h:X\to Y$ satisfying $ha=b$. It admits a simplicial model structure in which a morphism is a weak equivalence, cofibration or fibration exactly when its underlying arrow in $\mathcal M$ is one. Its initial object is $1_A:A\to A$ and its terminal object is $A\to1$, where $1$ is terminal in $\mathcal M$. Thus $a:A\to X$ is cofibrant as an object of $\mathcal M_{A/}$ exactly when $a$ is a cofibration, and is fibrant exactly when $X$ is fibrant in $\mathcal M$. For $a:A\to X$ and $b:A\to Y$, its enriched mapping simplicial set is the degreewise pullback
$$\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M_{A/}}(a,b)=\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(X,Y)\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(A,Y)}\{b\},$$
where the first map is precomposition with $a$ and $\{b\}:=\Delta^0\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(A,Y)$ is the vertex $b$. Its tensor of $a$ by a simplicial set $K$ is $A\to A\amalg_{A\otimes K}(X\otimes K)$, using $A\otimes K\to A$ induced by $K\to\Delta^0$; its cotensor of $b$ by $K$ is $A\to Y^K$, induced from $b$ by the constant-$K$ map $Y\to Y^K$. No properness or combinatorial hypothesis is required.

source.place: HTT Lemma A.3.7.1, proof, printed p. 907 (PDF p. 924), use of the simplicial model category of objects under A; the displayed enrichment and tensor/cotensor formulas are an agent-expansion of that construction. proof.text: Write $\mathcal U=\mathcal M_{A/}$. For a small diagram $D:J\to\mathcal U$, write its objects $a_j:A\to X_j$ and take $L=\lim_J X_j$ in $\mathcal M$, which exists by completeness in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. The compatible $a_j$ give $a:A\to L$. A cone from $z:A\to Z$ gives a unique underlying $h:Z\to L$; each projection of $hz$ is $a_j$, so uniqueness in the limit says $hz=a$. Conversely an arrow under $A$ supplies just such a cone. This proves the limit universal property, including the empty diagram, whose limit is $A\to1$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction: agent verification of simplicial-model foundations; limits in the ordinary undercategory

proof.text: For the same diagram set $B=\operatorname{colim}_J\operatorname{const}_J A$ and $T=\operatorname{colim}_J X_j$ in $\mathcal M$. The arrows $a_j$ induce $B\to T$, and the identity cocone on $A$ induces $B\to A$. Put $P=A\amalg_B T$, with structure arrow $A\to P$. By the cocone universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], a cocone under $A$ to $b:A\to Y$ is exactly a map $t:T\to Y$ for which $t(B\to T)=b(B\to A)$: this equality can be checked on every coprojection $A\to B$. Such pairs $(b,t)$ correspond uniquely to maps $P\to Y$ restricting to $b$. Hence $A\to P$ is the colimit. For $J$ empty both $B$ and $T$ are initial and $P=A$, giving initial object $1_A$. Completeness and cocompleteness of $\mathcal M$ supply all these objects; no connectedness assumption on $J$ is used.

proof.text: Define $C_{\mathcal U},F_{\mathcal U},W_{\mathcal U}$ by testing the underlying arrow in $\mathcal M$. Forgetting preserves composition and arrow-retract diagrams. The retract closure of all three classes and two-out-of-three for $W_{\mathcal U}$ therefore follow immediately from the model axioms in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization].

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction: agent verification of simplicial-model foundations; inherited retract and two-out-of-three axioms

proof.text: Given $h:(a:A\to X)\to(b:A\to Y)$, factor its underlying arrow functorially as $X\xrightarrow{l}Z\xrightarrow{r}Y$ in either ground weak factorization system. Give $Z$ the arrow $la:A\to Z$; then $rla=ha=b$, so this is a factorization under $A$ in the desired two classes. A commuting square between arrows under $A$ is a commuting square in $\mathcal M$; functoriality of the ground factorization makes the induced map $Z\to Z'$ commute with $la$ and $l'a'$. Thus both undercategory factorizations are functorial.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction: agent verification of simplicial-model foundations; both factorizations and their functoriality

proof.text: A square in $\mathcal U$ with left map $i:(a:A\to X)\to(a':A\to X')$ and right map $p:(b:A\to Y)\to(b':A\to Y')$ has top map $u:X\to Y$ and bottom map $v:X'\to Y'$. If the ground model lifting axiom supplies $h:X'\to Y$ with $hi=u$ and $ph=v$, then $ha'=hia=ua=b$. Thus this very lift lies in $\mathcal U$. Apply this to $(C_{\mathcal U},F_{\mathcal U}\cap W_{\mathcal U})$ and $(C_{\mathcal U}\cap W_{\mathcal U},F_{\mathcal U})$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction: agent verification of simplicial-model foundations; the diagonal lift automatically fixes the arrow from A

proof.text: For either pair $(L,R)$ just constructed, the lifting classes are exactly $L,R$, rather than merely containing them. Indeed, factor $h:X\to Y$ as $rl$ under $A$. If $h$ lifts on the left against every $R$-map, lifting against $r$ gives $d:Y\to Z$ with $dh=l$, $rd=1_Y$; the arrow maps $(1_X,d)$ and $(1_X,r)$ exhibit $h$ as an arrow retract of $l$. If $h$ lifts on the right against every $L$-map, lifting against $l$ gives $s:Z\to X$ with $sl=1_X$, $hs=r$; the arrow maps $(l,1_Y)$ and $(s,1_Y)$ exhibit $h$ as an arrow retract of $r$. All these maps are under $A$ by the lift calculation of the previous step. The retract closure checked in step 3 puts $h$ in $L$ or $R$, respectively. Together with steps 1-5 this verifies precisely the model-category axioms of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization].

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction: agent verification of simplicial-model foundations; explicit retract argument for the weak factorization systems

proof.text: The unique arrow $1_A\to(a:A\to X)$ has underlying map $a$, whereas the unique arrow $(a:A\to X)\to(A\to1)$ has underlying map $X\to1$. The definitions of cofibrant and fibrant in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] therefore give exactly the two stated characterizations. In particular cofibrancy of $A$ is irrelevant.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction: agent verification of simplicial-model foundations; initial/terminal maps and objectwise fibrancy/cofibrancy

proof.text: For $a:A\to X$ and $b:A\to Y$, define $U(a,b)$ to be the displayed strict pullback of simplicial sets. Its $n$-simplices are the $n$-simplices $f$ of $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(X,Y)$ whose restriction along $a$ is the constant $n$-simplex $b_n$. Faces and degeneracies preserve this equation. If $g\in U(b,c)_n$ and $f\in U(a,b)_n$, enriched composition in $\mathcal M$ satisfies $(gf)a=g(fa)=gb_n=c_n$. It consequently restricts to composition on these pullbacks. Identities restrict too, and associativity and unit equations are inherited. The vertices are exactly the ordinary arrows under $A$. Thus this is an enrichment of the ordinary category $\mathcal U$, with exactly the mapping formula asserted.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction: agent verification of simplicial-model foundations; the strict-fiber enrichment and all category laws

proof.text:
Let $K$ be a simplicial set, $c_Z:Z\otimes K\to Z$ the map induced by $K\to\Delta^0$, and $P=A\amalg_{A\otimes K}(X\otimes K)$, using $c_A$ and $a\otimes K$. We check the enriched tensor adjunction, not only its vertices. For any $V$, tensoring by $\Delta^n$ preserves a colimit: a map from its tensor to $V$ is, by tensor/cotensor adjunction, a map from that colimit to $V^{\Delta^n}$, hence a compatible family. Applying this to the pushout proves that $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(P,Y)$ is the simplicial pullback of $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(A,Y)$ and $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(X\otimes K,Y)$ over $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(A\otimes K,Y)$. Taking the strict fiber at $b$ over the first factor gives
$$U(A\to P,b)\cong\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(X\otimes K,Y)\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(A\otimes K,Y)}\{bc_A\}\cong U(a,b)^K.$$
The second identification is the ground enriched tensor adjunction: $bc_A$ transposes to the constant map $K\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(A,Y)$ at $b$. Exponentiation of a strict pullback of simplicial sets is the pullback of the exponentials, since a map $H\to E^K$ is exactly a map $H\times K\to E$ and the same equations define the pullback. These identifications commute with every map in $a,b,K$, giving the required enriched tensor and its functoriality.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction: agent verification of simplicial-model foundations; pushout tensor and its enriched adjunction

proof.text:
Give $Y^K$ the arrow $b_K:A\xrightarrow{b}Y\to Y^K$, where the second map is constant in $K$. The enriched cotensor adjunction in $\mathcal M$ identifies the restriction map $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(X,Y^K)\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(A,Y^K)$ with $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(X,Y)^K\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(A,Y)^K$, and identifies its distinguished vertex $b_K$ with $\operatorname{const}_K b$. Consequently
$$U(a,b_K)=\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(X,Y^K)\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(A,Y^K)}\{b_K\}\cong\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(X,Y)^K\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(A,Y)^K}\{\operatorname{const}_K b\}\cong U(a,b)^K.$$
For the last isomorphism, an $n$-simplex on either side is precisely a map $\Delta^n\times K\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(X,Y)$ whose composite with restriction along $a$ is constant at $b$; this description respects faces and degeneracies. Every identification is natural, since it uses only the ground natural adjunction and restriction maps, so it supplies the enriched cotensor adjunction and its functoriality. Write $T_K$ for the tensor of step 9 and $C_Kb=b_K$. For the unit, $T_{\Delta^0}a$ is $A\to A\amalg_A X\cong X$ and $C_{\Delta^0}b\cong b$. Iteration gives natural isomorphisms $U(T_L(T_Ka),b)\cong(U(a,b)^K)^L\cong U(a,b)^{L\times K}$ and $U(a,C_L(C_Kb))\cong(U(a,b)^K)^L\cong U(a,b)^{L\times K}$. Thus these objects represent $T_{L\times K}a$ and $C_{L\times K}b$, respectively. The representing isomorphisms give tensor and cotensor associativity; for three parameters both composites transpose to the identical map on $\Delta^n\times H\times L\times K$, so the associativity coherence holds, and deleting a $\Delta^0$ factor proves the unit coherence.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction: agent verification of simplicial-model foundations; cotensor by constants and its enriched adjunction

proof.text:
For a cofibration $i:a\to a'$ and fibration $p:b\to b'$ in $\mathcal U$, write their underlying maps $i:X\to X'$ and $p:Y\to Y'$. Ground SM7 in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] says that
$$\theta:\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(X',Y)\longrightarrow V:=\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(X,Y)\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(X,Y')}\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(X',Y')$$
is a Kan fibration, trivial if $i$ or $p$ is a weak equivalence. Put $T=U(a,b)\times_{U(a,b')}U(a',b')$, with its evident map $T\to V$. The preimage of $T$ under $\theta$ is exactly $U(a',b)$: in degree $n$, membership forces $(fi)a=b_n$, hence $fa'=b_n$ because $ia=a'$. Conversely $fa'=b_n$ implies $(fi)a=b_n$ and $(pf)a'=b'_n$, because $pb=b'$. The remaining equality in $T$ is just $p(fi)=(pf)i$. These checks commute with simplicial operators. Therefore the undercategory SM7 map $U(a',b)\to T$ is the pullback of $\theta$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction: agent verification of simplicial-model foundations; SM7 as an explicitly identified pullback

proof.text: By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], Kan fibrations and trivial Kan fibrations are characterized by right lifting against horns and boundaries, respectively. Any such lifting property is preserved under pullback: project a lifting square to the original map, choose a diagonal there, and pair that diagonal with the prescribed map to the new base; the commuting equation puts this pair in the pullback and proves both triangle equations. Hence the pullback map of step 11 is a Kan fibration, trivial whenever either input is a weak equivalence. This is exactly the simplicial-model axiom of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Together with the enrichment and adjunctions in steps 8-10 and the model structure in steps 1-7, it proves the statement, using no properness, combinatorial, or cofibrancy hypothesis on $A$.

lean.statement: theorem simplicial_undercategory_model (M : Type u) [Category.{v} M] [ModelCategory M] [HasLimits M] [HasColimits M] [MorphismProperty.HasFunctorialFactorization (cofibrations M) (trivialFibrations M)] [MorphismProperty.HasFunctorialFactorization (trivialCofibrations M) (fibrations M)] [SimplicialCategory M] (T : SimplicialTensorCotensor M) (_hSM7 : SatisfiesSM7 M) (A : M) : ∃ (m : ModelCategory (Under A)) (S : SimplicialCategory (Under A)) (U : @SimplicialTensorCotensor (Under A) _ S), HasLimits (Under A) ∧ HasColimits (Under A) ∧ MorphismProperty.HasFunctorialFactorization ((cofibrations M).inverseImage (Under.forget A)) ((trivialFibrations M).inverseImage (Under.forget A)) ∧ MorphismProperty.HasFunctorialFactorization ((trivialCofibrations M).inverseImage (Under.forget A)) ((fibrations M).inverseImage (Under.forget A)) ∧ @SatisfiesSM7 (Under A) _ m S ∧ (∀ (a b : Under A) (f : a ⟶ b), (m.categoryWithCofibrations.cofibrations f ↔ Cofibration f.right) ∧ (m.categoryWithFibrations.fibrations f ↔ Fibration f.right) ∧ (m.categoryWithWeakEquivalences.weakEquivalences f ↔ WeakEquivalence f.right)) ∧ Nonempty (IsInitial (Under.mk (𝟙 A))) ∧ Nonempty (IsTerminal (Under.mk (terminal.from A))) ∧ (∀ a : Under A, (m.categoryWithCofibrations.cofibrations (Under.homMk (U := Under.mk (𝟙 A)) (V := a) a.hom (by simp)) ↔ Cofibration a.hom) ∧ (m.categoryWithFibrations.fibrations (Under.homMk (U := a) (V := Under.mk (terminal.from A)) (terminal.from a.right) (by simp)) ↔ IsFibrant a.right)) ∧ (∃ e : ∀ a b : Under A, @sHom (Under A) _ S a b ≅ mappingFiber a b, MappingCompatibility S e) ∧ (∀ (a : Under A) (K : SSet.{v}), @SimplicialTensorCotensor.tensor (Under A) _ S U K a = tensorObject T K a) ∧ (∀ (b : Under A) (K : SSet.{v}), @SimplicialTensorCotensor.cotensor (Under A) _ S U K b = cotensorObject T K b)
